payload.reason: The evidence provides specific reasons why beam search is inadequate, including inefficiency in handling similar hypotheses and poor efficiency from pruning.

claims.text: Beam search is inadequate because it does not handle very similar hypotheses efficiently, leading to high overlap in outputs.
Most of the computation in beam search is not useful, as it produces a set of answers that does not contain most of the expanded nodes.
Beam search preserves similar outputs as different states, which limits its effectiveness in exploring diverse generation options.
